reference_sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers
FROM orders
WHERE order_ts >= DATE '2026-01-05' - INTERVAL 29 DAY
  AND order_ts < DATE '2026-01-05' + INTERVAL 1 DAY
alternatives: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers FROM orders WHERE CAST(order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-07' AND DATE '2026-01-05'

SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM (  -- one row per customer
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND order_ts >= DATE '2026-01-05' - INTERVAL 29 DAY
    AND order_ts < DATE '2026-01-05' + INTERVAL 1 DAY
) AS t

other_way.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM (  -- one row per customer
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND order_ts >= DATE '2026-01-05' - INTERVAL 29 DAY
    AND order_ts < DATE '2026-01-05' + INTERVAL 1 DAY
) AS t
other_way.tradeoff: Listing each customer once in a derived table shows the step, but COUNT(DISTINCT ...) does the same in one line.
